title: Route Diff Oracle & Auto-Rollback Simulation for Shadow and Canary Traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a Route Diff Oracle and a deterministic auto-rollback simulation sandbox to validate canary/A-B/shadow rollouts before they are promoted. The Oracle computes per-route cohort diffs (latency, token-accuracy proxies, top-k token distributions, rerank scores) and emits signal summaries and hypothesis-level confidence. The simulator replays historical traffic with shadowed variants and runs the same heuristic/ML rollback policies to estimate false-positive/false-negative rollback rates. This ticket scopes the PM/UX requirements, acceptance criteria, and cross-team coordination for engineering and design work.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-route cohort diff rows with delta, baseline CI, and alert severity
Simulator can replay N days of historical traffic and output simulated rollback decisions and root cause traces
Integrations: links to trace span IDs and GitHub PRs from simulated events
Threshold config UI available in rollout settings and persisted per-route

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Rather than shipping a full causal inference engine, start with signed deltas + configurable thresholds and a small ML classifier trained on past incidents. This reduces complexity and allows rapid iteration.
Simulator will run on an offline copy of production telemetry (pseudonymized) rather than live shadowing to avoid customer risk during initial experiments.
We will accept a small increase in telemetry storage (approx +12%) to capture per-token latency histograms; tradeoff accepted for richer rollback signal fidelity.

risks: Over-sensitive rollback policy may cause unnecessary rollbacks for noisy routes
Simulator fidelity depends on accuracy of offline traffic replay; mismatches in sampling could bias results
Large routes with very small deltas may require specialized statistical tests (we'll add A/B t-test fallback)
